* **Chief Complaint:** Pain in the top part of the right leg.

* **Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning:** Based on the patient's history and physical examination, it is likely that the patient has a soft tissue injury, possibly a contusion or strain, in the top part of her right leg. Further evaluation and imaging may be necessary to confirm the diagnosis.
* **Treatment Plan, Medications, and Follow-up:** The patient will be advised to rest the leg, apply ice, and elevate it to reduce swelling. Over-the-counter pain medication may be recommended to manage pain and discomfort. Follow-up with the healthcare provider will be necessary to assess the patient's progress and determine if further treatment is needed.

subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Pain in the top part of the right leg.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: Hello. I'm 43 years old, and I'm here because I hurt the top part of my right leg. I was bowling, and I accidentally hit my leg with the ball instead of the lane, and then I fell. It's been sore ever since. Doctor: Could you please provide your gender and describe the nature of the pain in your right leg, including when it started and if there is any swelling, bruising, or difficulty moving the leg? Patient: I'm female. The pain started when I hit my leg with the bowling ball, and it's been sore ever since. There's a little bruising on the back side of my leg, and it's swollen a little, but not too much. It's hard to walk on it, and I'm careful not to put too much weight on it. Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my right leg since the injury. It's just sore and bruised, and I'm careful not to put too much weight on it. Doctor: Have you had any prior injuries or surgeries to your right leg, and do you have any known medical conditions such as diabetes, osteoporosis, or blood clotting disorders? Patient: No, I haven't had any prior injuries or surgeries to my right leg. I do have a history of atopic eczema, and I had a colectomy in the past due to diverticulitis, but that was on my abdomen, not my leg. I don't have diabetes, osteoporosis, or any blood clotting disorders that I'm aware of. Doctor: Could you describe the exact location of the pain on your right leg and whether you've noticed any deformity or instability in the area? Patient: The pain is on the top part of my right leg, more on the side.
